content: The Eisenhower Medical Center, located in Rancho Mirage, California, is the only not-for-profit hospital in the Coachella Valley. It was recognized as one of the top 100 hospitals in the United States in 2005 and is home to the renowned Betty Ford Center. As of 2006, the facility operates as a General Acute Care Hospital with Basic Emergency Services. The hospital is named after President Dwight D. Eisenhower and owes its inception to two pivotal events in 1966. Entertainer Bob Hope was asked to lend his name to a charity golf tournament, which still bears his name, and to serve on the board of the hospital that would be funded by the tournament's proceeds. Due to his busy schedule, Bob Hope suggested his wife, Dolores Hope, take on the role instead. Dolores, an accomplished philanthropist, agreed and has served as President, Chairman of the Board, and Chairman Emeritus since 1968, playing a key role in every major decision regarding the hospital. The original 80 acres of land for the hospital were donated by Bob and Dolores Hope, who also helped raise private funds for its construction. Prominent figures in American entertainment and politics, including Ronald Reagan, Frank Sinatra, George Burns, Bing Crosby, Gene Autry, and Lucille Ball, contributed their time to fundraisers and dedication ceremonies. Two months after the groundbreaking, Dolores Hope established the Eisenhower Medical Center Auxiliary, which has since become one of the most successful volunteer organizations of its kind globally. Bob Hope served as the master of ceremonies for the hospital's opening in November 1971. Several medical buildings were named in honor of local philanthropists, including Mr. and Mrs. Walter Probst, Mr. and Mrs. Peter Kiewit, and Mrs. Hazel Wright. Bob Hope also presided over the opening of the 47-bed Mamie Eisenhower Wing. The hospital underwent significant expansion during the 1980s, with the Hopes attending every major event and opening despite their demanding schedules. Their involvement included the planning and inaugurations of the Annenberg Center for Health Sciences, the Betty Ford Center, the Barbara Sinatra Children’s Center, the Dolores Hope Outpatient Care Center, and the Uihlein Administration Building. By 1990, the hospital had performed its 3,000th open-heart surgery. The Hopes' dedication to the Eisenhower Medical Center earned them international recognition and numerous honors, including a combined total of 60 honorary doctorates. In 1996, during the hospital's 25th anniversary, the Hopes received its highest honor, the Eisenhower Centennial Award. In January 2006, the Eisenhower Medical Center gained global attention when President Gerald Ford was admitted for 16 days to treat pneumonia. Following his death on December 26, 2006, his body was taken to the hospital, where Betty Ford issued a press release confirming his passing. His body remained at the hospital until the commencement of funeral services on December 29.
